author: Aaronjacobs000
summary: These parsers read 1Password Business sign-in attempts, item usage and audit events from the 1Password Events API. The example bridge in bridges/1password-events pulls the records and posts them to HTTP Ingest. Sign-in attempts go to Auth, and item usage and audit events go to CloudAudit.
notes:
Setup:
- 1Password has no syslog or webhook for these events, so these parsers read records pulled from the 1Password Events API by the example bridge in bridges/1password-events and posted to HTTP Ingest.
- The bridge names each record's feature in onepassword_record.

Field mapping:
- Sign-in attempts go to Auth, with the category (success, credentials_failed, mfa_failed, sso_failed, firewall_failed and others) as the result and the type as the detail.
- Item usage (reveal, fill, secure-copy, export, share and server changes) and audit events (vault, group, user, MFA, SSO and firewall changes) go to CloudAudit.
- An audit event's name is its object type and action, such as user.suspend.

Made up in the samples:
- Samples follow the object shapes in 1Password's Events API reference with made-up values.

Testing:
- Each child, combined with the parent into one parser, passed Run Test in a lab tenant on 2026-10-14 (138 of 138 fields matched the emulator, including a nanosecond and an offset timestamp), and the parent's confirm string picked the same records there.
- Each child also passed Run Test as a separate parser under its parent.
- No built-in parser claimed these records in 10 Run Tests.
